en.headline: Health officials warn of risks from cadaver-derived beauty injections after raids
en.dek: The Department of Health seized unregistered Elravie Re2O products that claim to contain human tissue and arrested a woman, citing lack of clinical safety data.
body: The Department of Health has warned of public health risks from an unregistered Korean beauty injection known as Elravie Re2O, which claims to contain human tissue, after raids on beauty premises and the arrest of a woman.

According to the department, officers searched four premises in Tsim Sha Tsui, Mong Kok, Tsuen Wan and Yuen Long on 16 and 20 October. In the Tsim Sha Tsui and Mong Kok locations they seized more than 100 vials of suspected Part 1 poisons and more than 70 vials of suspected unregistered pharmaceutical products, including 20 vials of Elravie Re2O. A 38-year-old woman was arrested on suspicion of illegal possession of poisons and unregistered pharmaceuticals, and of illegally dealing in human organs for commercial purposes.

Dr Fung Ying, Controller of the Department of Health’s Regulatory Affairs division, said the product’s packaging claims it contains human tissue, placing it under both the Human Organ Transplant Ordinance as a regulated product and the Pharmacy and Poisons Ordinance as a pharmaceutical product. The department has received exemption applications for the regulated product but has not granted any, and has received no registration application for the pharmaceutical product. She said the items lack clinical safety data and pose public health risks.

The department has reminded doctors and private healthcare institutions that the sale or possession of unregistered pharmaceutical products is unlawful. It stressed that any injection procedure is a medical procedure that should only be performed by a locally registered doctor or registered dentist, and advised the public to verify practitioners’ credentials before accepting such treatments.

zh.headline: 衞生署警告屍皮針有公共衞生風險 突擊搜查後拘捕女子
zh.dek: 署方在四間美容處所檢獲未經註冊的Elravie Re2O針劑，聲稱含人類組織，並指產品缺乏臨床安全數據。
body: 衞生署警告，一款聲稱含有人類組織的韓國美容針劑Elravie Re2O（俗稱屍皮針）缺乏臨床安全數據，有公共衞生風險。署方近日突擊搜查多間美容處所並拘捕一名女子。
衞生署表示，於10月16日及20日搜查尖沙咀、旺角、荃灣及元朗四間提供美容服務的處所。在尖沙咀及旺角處所內，檢獲超過100支懷疑第1部毒藥針劑及超過70支懷疑未經註冊的藥劑製品針劑，當中包括20支Elravie Re2O。一名38歲女子因涉嫌非法管有第1部毒藥及未經註冊藥劑製品，以及涉嫌非法將人體器官作商業交易被警方拘捕。
規管事務總監封螢醫生指出，該產品包裝聲稱含有人類組織，既屬《人體器官移植條例》下的受規管產品，亦受《藥劑業及毒藥條例》規管為藥劑製品。署方早前接獲相關受規管產品的豁免申請，仍在處理中，至今未批出任何豁免，亦不曾接獲該產品的藥劑製品註冊申請。她表示有關產品缺乏臨床安全數據，有公共衞生風險。
署方已去信全港醫生及私營醫療機構，提醒非法售賣或管有未經註冊藥劑製品屬違法。署方強調，注射程序屬醫療程序，只應由本地註冊醫生或註冊牙醫施行，市民接受前應核實從業者資格。
